summary.assessment: The model is reliable only on a single-panel chart whose numbers are printed and large (B1: 12 of 12 counts exact) and gives usable eyeball estimates on a simple single-panel forest plot (B4: all centres within 2 % of the range); the third correct figure, C5, was read by the engine's vector pie reader without calling the model. Its typical failure is structural: every multi-panel data figure except C1 was merged into one panel or only partly read (B2, B3, B5, C3, C4), which loses whole panels (120 of 180 values in B2, 27 of 30 in B5, 16 of 24 in C4, all 264 in C3) and attaches values to the wrong panel, model name or axis. Where it places marks for the engine to measure, the marks are not on the data (C1: 9 of 12 bars read 0.04-0.24 too low because the marks sit inside the bars; A3: centres 0.02-0.04 low), and interval ends, whisker tops and outliers come back as extra plain values (A3, B5, C4). Small printed text is unsafe: 6 of 15 AUROC labels in B3 were misread and percent turned into fractions. On figures without data it declined three diagrams, leaving only empty panel shells, but invented a line series for ECG traces (A5, 102 rows, 632 s) and took a worked example's output as data (C2). Several of the scorer's zeros (A3, C1, C4) are naming or pairing mismatches that overstate the error, but the underlying extractions are still not usable as they are: trust it on single-panel charts with printed values, and not on multi-panel, measured or dense figures.
